rationale: Round 0 compiled and ran correctly, so I shift weights toward stronger obfuscation while respecting that fp-convert is a 584-byte, 3-function binary with hot floating-point loops where runtime overhead is the main constraint. SUB stays the workhorse: instruction substitution is nearly free at runtime and size, so its high SecurityGain/DiversityGain weights and low cost weights make it applicable everywhere. SPLIT gets a strong DiversityGain weight because basic-block splitting composes cheaply with the other passes and this program is too small to protect via volume alone. FLA and BCF carry the bulk of control-flow disguise but their elevated RuntimeCost weights keep them from being forced onto the hot FP conversion loops; their moderate CorrectnessRisk weights stay low since round 0 showed no instability. IBR and ICALL raise branch/call indirection for static-analysis resistance with mid-range cost tolerance. IGV adds global indirection at low cost given the tiny data section. No passes are disabled — the cost weights, not omissions, gate the expensive transforms.
